reason: Quote states that in Firewall Manager-managed web ACLs individual accounts can manage their own rules and rule groups in addition to the policy's rule groups.
Quote under 'General settings' (settings common to all policies) states you can view out-of-compliance accounts and resources without corrective action or automatically remediate.
Quote states that for a new account added to the organization, Firewall Manager automatically applies the policy to in-scope resources in that account.
Quote states Firewall Manager is particularly useful for protecting the entire organization or when frequently adding new resources, and provides centralized DDoS attack monitoring.

Doc-history row dated April 25, 2024 announces network ACL policies; the policy page quote says Firewall Manager enforces the presence and ordering of the policy's first and last rules in in-scope network ACLs.
Doc-history row dated May 5, 2023 states policies per organization rose from 20 to 50, primary security groups per policy from one to three, and the WCU maximum became a hard quota.
Doc-history row dated October 22, 2024 states Firewall Manager AWS WAF policies can now retrofit existing account-owned web ACLs and create new ones only where needed.
Claim is the verbatim guide note. Writers should pair it with firewall-manager-policy-fee: the pricing page also charges a monthly fee per policy per Region.
Quote states compliance status is viewable for all policies and an account or resource is compliant when the policy settings are reflected in its settings.
Quote states AWS Config must continuously record changes for protected resources and the recording frequency must be Continuous, which is the default.
Pricing page states Firewall Manager creates two AWS Config rules per policy, per account (repeated in every policy-type example), and those Config rules are charged at current pricing.
Quotes define full administrative scope as all accounts and OUs, all Regions and all policy types, and state the default administrator can manage third-party firewalls.
FAQ quote states Firewall Manager is a security management service to centrally configure and manage firewall rules across accounts and applications in AWS Organizations.
Quotes state DNS Firewall filters outbound DNS traffic for VPCs and the policy creates an association between each rule group and each in-scope VPC for each in-scope account.
FAQ quotes describe automatic remediation (monitors drift, applies rules to non-compliant resources) and manual remediation (creates policy and rules in each account without enforcing them).
FAQ quote under 'Which AWS resources can AWS Firewall Manager configure rules on?' states you can configure new VPC network ACLs for VPC subnets.
FAQ quotes state Firewall Manager can deploy Network Firewalls across accounts and VPCs and associate Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rules across VPCs in the organization.
Claim is the verbatim FAQ sentence, including 'at this time'.
FAQ quotes state Firewall Manager must be associated with the management account or a permitted member account, and that account is called the Firewall Manager administrator account.
FAQ quote states you can configure new VPC security groups and audit existing ones for EC2, ALB and ENI resource types.
FAQ quote lists Shield Advanced protections for ALBs, ELB Classic Load Balancers, Elastic IP addresses and CloudFront distributions.
FAQ quotes state SNS channels give real-time notifications for new non-compliant resources and each in-scope account is notified of non-compliant events on Security Hub.
FAQ quote states WAF rules can be rolled out across Application Load Balancer, API Gateways and CloudFront distributions.

The quote supports findings for out-of-compliance resources and detected attacks sent to Security Hub CSPM. 'Automatically when you use both services' is only in the next, unquoted sentence; add it as evidence.
Pricing quote states the protection policy is included at no additional charge for Shield Advanced customers, who are still charged for the AWS Config rules created.
Quotes state only the management account can create default administrator accounts, and Firewall Manager sets the default administrator as an Organizations delegated administrator.
FAQ quote states manual remediation creates the policy and rules in each account without enforcing them, and you can later edit the policy to remediate automatically.
Hard-quota table row gives 10 administrators per organization: one default plus up to nine more. The Hard quotas section quote says these can't be changed.

The quote supports one or multiple administrators and scope conditions per administrator. The list 'accounts or OUs, Regions and policy types' is not in the quote or its context; it appears in the page's 'Administrative scope' bullets, which should be added as evidence.
The quote is a soft (default, increase-requestable) quota of 5 inbound and 5 outbound first-or-last rules per policy. The claim's 'at most 5' states it as a fixed maximum; it should say 'by default'.
Quotes state the account must be a member of the organization and the organization must be enabled for all features; the context names consolidated billing as the other, insufficient feature set.

The quotes support managing Network Firewall firewalls across the organization based on a firewall management type. The three models (distributed, centralized, import) and their descriptions are only in the unquoted bullet list; add those bullets as evidence.

Quotes support that rule groups must already exist in the administrator account and that the policy shares rule groups across accounts. The must-claim 'you must have resource sharing enabled for AWS Organizations' is in the unquoted next sentence; add it as evidence.

The quote supports that protections are not removed unless the check box is selected. The fact's condition (the option is not available for Shield Advanced or AWS WAF Classic policies) is a cannot-claim found only in the unquoted Note; add it as evidence.
FAQ quote states policies are Region specific, each can include only resources in its Region, and you create a policy for each Region where you operate.

Quotes support a monthly fee per policy per Region and $100 per month in pricing example 1. The condition 'some Regions charge more than $100' comes from a page Note that no quote includes; add that line as evidence.

The quote supports one policy type per policy, multiple policies for multiple types, and more than one policy per type. The parenthesized list of seven policy types is not quoted; it is in the page's type bullets, which should be added.

Quotes support three mandatory and one optional prerequisite, Organizations with all features, and AWS Config on member accounts. The administrator account and the optional AWS RAM sharing item are only in unquoted context.
Soft-quota row gives a default of 3 primary security groups per policy; the May 5, 2023 doc-history row says the maximum increased from one to three.
Quote states Firewall Manager simplifies administration across multiple accounts and resources for WAF, Shield Advanced, VPC security groups and network ACLs, Network Firewall and DNS Firewall.
